draft.title: Antibiotic resistance
card: Antibiotics are drugs that kill bacteria or stop them growing. They do not work on viruses.
In a large bacterial population, a random mutation may give a few cells a resistant allele. The mutation is not caused by the antibiotic.
When the antibiotic is used, it kills susceptible bacteria. Resistant bacteria survive, reproduce and pass on the resistant allele.
Over generations, the resistant allele becomes more common in the population. This is natural selection, with the antibiotic as the selection pressure.
draft.remember: The antibiotic does not create resistance. It selects for resistant bacteria that already exist.

a.q: A patient takes an antibiotic and most of the bacteria die. A few survive and multiply. Why are the survivors resistant?
opts: They already carried an allele that gave resistance
They changed their DNA to cope with the antibiotic
They were exposed to the drug and learned to resist it
They took in the drug and became stronger over time
a.why: The resistant allele was already present in a few cells, from a random mutation. The antibiotic killed the susceptible cells, so the resistant ones survived and reproduced. It did not make the bacteria change on purpose.
a.clue: Did the resistant allele appear before or after the drug was used?

b.q: A hospital ward uses the same antibiotic on many patients for a year. The share of resistant bacteria on the ward rises. Which explanation is best?
opts: Resistant bacteria survived and reproduced more than others
Each bacterium slowly became resistant during its own life
The drug caused new resistant alleles to form in the bacteria
Susceptible bacteria chose to become resistant to the drug
b.why: Resistant bacteria lived through each course of the drug and left more offspring, so the resistant allele became more common. This is natural selection. The tempting option about the drug causing new alleles is wrong, because mutations arise at random and the drug only selects among them.
b.clue: Think about which bacteria are left to reproduce after each course.
